L01.text: The shortest war in history lasted about thirty-eight minutes. You've had longer phone calls.

L02.text: Zanzibar, August eighteen ninety-six. The sultan dies, and his cousin Khalid moves into the palace without asking Britain first.

L03.text: Britain disagrees. It parks warships in the harbour, and sends a note: leave by nine o'clock tomorrow morning.

L04.text: Khalid barricades the palace, and waits.

L05.text: Nine o'clock arrives. The ships open fire.

L06.text: The palace catches fire. And the sultan's entire navy, one royal yacht, sinks in the harbour.

L07.text: Khalid? He slips out the back, and hides in the German consulate.

L08.text: By about nine forty, the guns stop. A new sultan is in charge before lunch.

L09.text: Short, but not painless. Hundreds were hurt in the palace.

L10.text: Luckily, it was over before breakfast went cold. Unluckily, the losing side was sent the bill for the shells.

L11.text: Thirty-eight minutes. Still the shortest war ever recorded.
